ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The image is a schematic diagram of the locust life cycle, with multiple locust forms arranged in a circle along arrows. On the right there is a group of eggs labeled A, after which an arrow points to a smaller nymph, then to a larger nymph. The B on the left is located beside a larger immature locust; it is after several smaller nymph stages, and there is an arrow from the locust near B continuing to point to the fully developed adult labeled E above. Reasoning: The question asks what stage locust B is. According to the life cycle order in the diagram, B is the last nymph stage before adult E. Locusts go through successive nymph instars before becoming adults, and the last nymph instar is the 5th instar nymph. Therefore, locust B is 5th Stage Nymph.
